units.summary: The aggregate backend's ReverseProxy now sets FlushInterval to -1, so every write is flushed to the client immediately. This changes streaming behavior for responses that carry a Content-Length.
units.headline: Aggregate proxy now flushes after every write
units.reason: Changes ReverseProxy flushing, which affects streaming and buffering of all aggregated responses.
focus: Responses with Content-Length are now flushed per write, which may cost throughput on large bodies

units.summary: The forward backend's ReverseProxy now sets FlushInterval to -1, so every write is flushed immediately. Watch events are no longer at the mercy of the Content-Length heuristic.
units.headline: Forward proxy now flushes after every write
units.reason: Changes ReverseProxy flushing, which affects streaming and buffering of all forwarded responses.
focus: Responses with Content-Length are now flushed per write, which may cost throughput on large bodies

units.summary: Adds a constant of -1 that is passed to ReverseProxy.FlushInterval in the forward, aggregate and single-tenant proxies. It has no effect on its own. The comment's claim holds for ReverseProxy, and in-process backends are not proxies.
units.headline: New streamingFlushInterval constant set to -1
units.reason: A constant definition only. The behavior change is in the units that use it.

units.summary: The breakers cache now stores *groupBreaker, an alias for gobreaker's two-step breaker, instead of the one-step breaker. This is a type change that follows the PR's breaker rework.
units.headline: ST fallback breaker cache holds two-step breakers
units.reason: A field type change that follows the alias, with no logic change here. The behavior change is in breaker.go.

units.summary: The LRU cache for breakers is constructed with the *groupBreaker element type. Only the type parameter changes.
units.headline: Breaker LRU now built with groupBreaker type
units.reason: Only the generic type argument changed, and it matches the field type.

units.summary: The single-tenant fallback's ReverseProxy now sets FlushInterval to -1, so it flushes after every write. Watches through the ST fallback stream regardless of Content-Length.
units.headline: ST fallback proxy now flushes after every write
units.reason: Changes ReverseProxy flushing, which affects streaming of all single-tenant fallback responses.
focus: Responses with Content-Length are now flushed per write, which may cost throughput on large bodies

units.summary: The return type changes to *groupBreaker, matching the cache's new element type. The key and locking logic are unchanged.
units.headline: breakerForDestination returns groupBreaker type
units.reason: A signature type change that follows the alias, with the body untouched. Callers' breaker usage is in other units.
